 Iowa sees record early voting ahead of Election Day 
 By Eric Min Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 5:43 PM CST | Updated : 11 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google DES MOINES, Iowa (KTTC) – In an interview with KTTC Monday, Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate said the Hawkeye State has seen a record amount of early voting, well above the amount four years ago. State election data showed that more than 482,000 ballots had been requested early.
 “This is not typical,” Pate said. “I think it has a lot to do with having an open governor’s race, a U.S. Senate race, several congressional races, constitutional amendments, and a lot of local races.”
 According to Pate, 70% of early voting took place in person, a statistic that he said is substantially higher than four years ago.
 “Turn on your TV and you’ll see a political ad,” Pate said. “A lot of commercials out there messaging that it is important people get out and vote. I think those all contribute to it, and Iowa and Minnesota have a great record when it comes to voter participation.”
 As a reminder to Iowa voters, Pate said you can no longer have an attestor verify your identity before you vote. He is asking community members not to forget their ID cards.
 “If you’re in line before 8 o’clock, you will be given a chance to vote,” Pate said. “I don’t care how long the line is, they will stay there until those folks get a chance to have their vote cast.”
